content: Web smiles. "Thank you. Web love you too."
"Family."
They smile softly and press a kiss to their forehead. “Make sure you get some real sleep, okay? I’ll see you in the morning.”
Leaf walks in, appreciating the open door. Not taking notice of John, she walks to the center of the pub and turns in a 360 to look it over. "Not so bad when it's quiet..." She says to herself.
Web nods. "Feels good not being one taking care of others. Nice to be taken care of sometimes." They step back, still happy crying.
They give them a warm smile. “We’ve got a difficult few days ahead. But I believe in us.”
"Not so bad with conversation neither, lass"
The tables and chairs disappear. Web nods happily as the scene begins to fade. "If Web ever afraid of Wynne again, can do something for me?"

He thinks about promises. He thinks about marriages. He thinks about if he had parents. He thinks about the orphanage. The broth. The sunken faces. He thinks about the sisters and how hungry they had looked. He thinks about the Mask. He hadn't liked what it had made him think about. How tempting it was. He thinks about his new rapier for a while.
They nod. “Anything.”

Web holds their hands out in front of them, palms turned down. They breathe in, drawing their palms together and up in a praying position. They breathe out, moving their hands back to the original position but palm-up. "Do that, and say 'Kraoli' at end. Druidic for 'dream'. Will help remember this moment, center self. Can Wynne do that?"

Leaf jumps a bit "Oh! Sorry, didn't see you there." She looks a bit embarrassed "And you're probably right. I've only been in a place like this once before and it was all the way back in London. Figured I might as well visit before whatever happens on Friday."
Wynne mimicks the motion a few times and nods. “Kraoli. Will remember.”
Web smiles to them and nods. "Thank you." Web steps back and the dream ends.
Web exits their trance and smiles to Baeshra. "Good talk with Wynne." They give Baeshra a small kiss and settle in for the night.
Wynne sleeps with a smile on their face for the rest of the night.
The rest of Wynne's sleep will remain peaceful and calm. They will remember the dream with perfect clarity.
Baeshra nods and goes to ask a question. But she's adapting to Web spacing out and getting other things done. Baeshra continues to stare at the rabbit confused for a while.
Web falls asleep quickly. "Have good sleep, Apex."

Early on the morning, Florian ( <@!360967589511561218> ) knocks on Goose’s door with a stack of elementary schoolbooks. Goose opens the door to see Florian’s expression of wholesome giddiness. Which changes quickly, as Goose stands there in the pinkest frilliest apron paired with the darkest undereye (can Aaracokras have dark under eyes?). Goose doesn’t notice how strange their attire is.
Selene notices skitter in the branches and wren upon the mattress and gauges the benefits if sleep vs. studying weighing both in their mind

.
They’re expression changes to happiness upon seeing Florian and invites him in. After a quick exchange, Florian gets promptly seated with a hot chocolate, madeleine, and crepes. Goose sits across him and stares. Their gaze quickly switches from Florian to the platter. Florian gives his hearty French laugh and samples each dessert. Goose watches, with bated breath.

.
Although ultimately, Florian liked them- it was not the reaction Goose wanted (got okayish rolls :/ ) . Before Goose asks suggestions on how to improve, they’re met face to face with a book
```Phonics with Florian```
(will Goose read with a French accent then?) XD
"I notice you've not quite said what your considerin? Is it some thin that happened here? Or back in London?"

Of course, Goose tries to remind him that ‘they’re Goose, 19-’, Florian gives his usual charming smile as he tells Goose he’s gonna teach him how to read. Before Goose can even form a syllable, Florian (metaphysically) drags them along for the wonderful world of reading and writing. A flurry of alphabets, words, and grammar is bombed onto the unsuspecting bird. Goose is now slightly disheveled, trying to keep their writing fast enough for ‘class’. Another new letter, another word, another “sound”. Florian keeps a perfect smile as Goose tries to attempt a crawl to escape. “Reading its fundamental!” rings out as Goose is pulled back.

.
A distressing honk can be heard.
Goose levels up in reading and writing!

.
Goose thanks Florian profusely and profess how much more confident they feel. Florian stand a little taller with hand on his lapels “I will return tomorrow with more advanced lessons!” Goose lets him know a platter of French treats will be waiting for him. Saying their goodbyes, Goose turns around. Before they can head back inside, they notice scratches on the dirt of their doorway. Whatever made those scratches seemed really desperate to leave. Goose looks closely at the marks, their detective instinct active. Unfortunately, that instinct is pretty bad so they just shrug and ignore it.

.
Despite Goose still rocking them e-girl red eyeshadow undereye, they stretch, yawn, and start a big day. “Man, a business is something you really got to work for.” Goose thought as they sit at their desk. They ponder a bit on what else they should do. Practice baking? Goose think they deserve a break. Learn new recipes? They think on it and figured they should use their new reading skills to the test. They open Florian’s gift and with a stunning roll of...2 (ASKAJSKJ BRO THE DC WAS 7) their cumulative exhaustion from bake-a-thon and ‘Phonics with Florian’, causes words to blur before their eyes. They immediately close the book and hold their head in their hands.

.
They’ll admit it, they took a nap- but it wasn’t long before <@!321508500138360843>  knocked. Except, their politeness didn't wake up Goose right away. It kept on escalating to a point where Selene just sighs and leaves a note.

.
You know who isn't afraid to be not-polite? <@!260820438026813440> . Just when Selene leaves Web comes along, eager to pass along what they learned from Bashara. They pick up Selene's note, and kindly starts banging on the doors. Web hears what they think is Goose saying “I DONT WANNA LEARN WHAT RHYMES WITH CAT!!!” After a little while, the door cracks open a little bit. Upon seeing Web, Goose opens the door wide and welcomes them.

.
Goose puts down a ```tw for gross old food``` ||a chartruise board of weevil infested hardtack, jerky with white stuff, moldy dried fruit, and a spoiled fruit jam with fermented rice|| for Web. They even give a couple breads on the go, so web can wait until they’re ‘aged’. They have a lovely conversation, and Goose tells Web all about their adventures yesterday and even proudly present their notes last night. Web easily reads the notes, as they understand the simple grammar- even so they get confused on some parts, where goose happily jumps in and clarifies. 
.
Once Web heard and read about the macaron and meat crepe incident they decided they gotta take control. They lead Goose over to the kitchen and start to guide them on the precision of baking macarons; from the exact grams to the exact handiwork. Although tired, Goose happily learns. Of course, Goose is very grateful of the cookbook, they figure they rather learn by experience then reading - at least at the moment.

.
The process takes up a lot of time. Web wouldn’t let up until Goose made a perfect batch. Even when that’s achieved Web excited shows Goose how a meat crepe would work. They would need to prepare the meat to be as tender as possible, as well as a sauce that will compliment the meat and bring in the whole crepe.

.
‘So throwing jerky at a crepe isn't gonna cut it’ goose figures

.
When Web looked at the time, they excused themself- but not without reassuring Goose that they shouldn’t be shy when it comes to asking for help. Goose invites them to the back of the store for more ‘aged’ morsels. Before they forget Web leaves Goose with Selene's note and a couple words of encouragement.

.
Goose ogles at their perfect macaron. They tentively grab a piece like if it was glass baby. (UNLIKE glass babies) Goose takes a bite out of the treat. Their mouth sings at the marinades of textures. It reminds them of those pink cloud like candy they used to see children carry after a town carnival. Unfortunately, whenever they got their beak on one and take it back to their lake, the cloud disappears? But this, this is what goose always thought it would taste like. They look at the rest of the failed/unappealing batches. They have to admit today’s taste testing made them feel like that was enough sweets for a goose (think eating a Cadbury crème egg; just a assault of sugar).

.
The door opens and Goose gets attacked with a barrage of children screaming “IT’S MR DUCK!!!” After the giggles and tomfoolery, Goose laughs it off and produces many boxes tired with colored twine. Inside was the result of all the extra baking of all types of crepes, madeleines, breads with topping, and macarons. The orphanage caretaker scolds Goose for the hyperactivity of the kids from all the sugar, but her eyes shine- clearly happy for the children to smile. While the children snack, Goose tells them their adventures (with all the gory and inappropriate bits left out). They let children use him as a playground, hanging from their biceps and try to jump touch “Mr. Duck’s” head. They show off their wings to the orphan’s request, and explain how bird fly (no, it not *magic*...at least not all the time). One of their favorite things to do is to read them bed time stories; its good practice for Goose’s vocabulary and reading skills. (Also Goose would totally join in on nap time)

.
They get home VERY exhausted, but still happy. As they clean up the kitchen, they notice two small jars. They forgot what they out it in. They dip a finger in and tasted it. The moment they swallowed, their exhaustion felt lighter - its not gone - but it is significantly lighter. They stare at it, and suddenly shoot up - to go to bed because they need rest, but they plan to do some serious research the next day… and figure out how to make candied flowers.

.
Goose dreams of shrunken in a field of candied flowers.
